iterations.explanation: Chosen dimensions separate gateway routing scope, client-specific decomposition, repository ownership/data access, and event-based propagation. No user feedback existed, so none needed incorporation. Q2: Addressed axis-vs-value by making each dimension an architectural concern type, orthogonal to others.

clusters.name: API Gateway Request Routing Responsibility
clusters.description: Documents vary by how much request-routing logic the gateway owns (full routing to services vs gateway only delegating). Orthogonal to data, repos, client tailoring, and events.

clusters.name: Client-Specific Service Decomposition
clusters.description: Documents differ in whether PC and mobile use separate backend services for tailored responses. This is orthogonal to routing responsibility and repository/data-access patterns.

clusters.name: Repository Separation and SQL Data Ownership
clusters.description: Documents vary in repository boundaries for SQL access during migration (separate customer vs order repositories, per-service repositories). Orthogonal to gateway routing and event propagation.

clusters.name: In-Service Data Access via Per-Service Repositories
clusters.description: Documents specify that each microservice uses its own repository layer for SQL operations, including customer-related modules. Orthogonal to general repository separation and distinct from gateway routing decisions.

clusters.name: Internal State Propagation via Events
clusters.description: Documents differ in using observer/event mechanisms for propagating internal state changes to statistics components. Orthogonal to synchronous request routing and to repository topology.

clusters.name: API Exposure and Contract Management for Data Services
clusters.description: Documents vary by gateway role in exposing and managing APIs for customer/order data services. Orthogonal to whether the gateway performs routing only or owns tailoring logic.

iterations.explanation: I preserved existing dimensions for routing responsibility, client decomposition, repository topology, event-based state propagation, and API/contract exposure. New batch added three orthogonal concerns not previously covered: external third-party integration (Payments adapter vs routing), business resilience (limited retries), and facade/statistics aggregation (fits API exposure/contract management rather than routing). Kept repository split (separation vs per-service ownership) and expanded event dimension to include event sourcing examples.

iterations.explanation: The taxonomy already covers all review-sample themes with orthogonal axes: gateway routing, client-specific decomposition, repository ownership vs access layering, event-based state propagation, API exposure/contracting, external third-party integration patterns, resilience/retry for business workflows, monolith decomposition boundaries, and distinct delivery/routing selection vs plugin vs modularization strategies. No changes made because dimensions map cleanly to each sample item without overlapping intent, and there is no catch-all category or missing major axis for the stated migration use case (PC/mobile, customers/orders SQL, delivery optimization, payments, retries, events).
